skill.name: distributed-debugging-debug-trace
skill.description: Configure distributed debugging, tracing, logging, profiling, and diagnostic workflows for development and production systems.
skill.summary: Set up practical debugging and observability workflows across services.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from JavaScript template literals, Markdown formatting, and normal process.env configuration reads. Confirmed risks remain in the remote debugger, request-body trace attributes, unsafe dashboard innerHTML, hostname logging, and profile or heap files. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Remote debugging binds to public interfaces and evaluates client-supplied expressions.
remediation.suggestion: Bind inspector and debug WebSocket ports to localhost, require strong authentication, use secure tunnels, and disable this path in production by default.

remediation.issue: Tracing examples capture request bodies and identity fields.
remediation.suggestion: Remove raw request bodies from spans and redact or hash user and session identifiers before export.

remediation.issue: Dashboard examples insert debug payloads with innerHTML.
remediation.suggestion: Use textContent, safe DOM construction, or a vetted sanitizer for all WebSocket-delivered metrics, traces, and log messages.

remediation.issue: CPU profiles and heap snapshots are written to local files.
remediation.suggestion: Store profiling outputs in restricted directories, encrypt or protect access, and define retention and cleanup rules.

remediation.issue: Production debug context can expose runtime information.
remediation.suggestion: Require short-lived tokens, narrow IP allow lists, audit logging, and explicit incident windows for production debugging.

semantic_findings.title: Unauthenticated Remote Debug Execution
semantic_findings.description: The remote debug server opens the Node inspector on 0.0.0.0, creates a WebSocket server without authentication, and passes received expressions to Runtime.evaluate. This can allow remote code execution if exposed.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines bind the inspector broadly, accept unauthenticated WebSocket messages, route evaluate commands, and pass client-supplied expressions to Runtime.evaluate.

semantic_findings.title: Sensitive Data Captured in Traces
semantic_findings.description: The OpenTelemetry hooks add request bodies, user IDs, and session IDs to spans. Exporting these spans can expose credentials or personal data to tracing backends.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code explicitly adds request.body, user.id, and session.id to telemetry attributes, which are commonly sensitive in production systems.

semantic_findings.title: Production Debug Context Exposure
semantic_findings.description: The production debugging middleware can enable request debug mode, capture console output, and attempt to return exported debug context in a response header. Weak tokens or broad IP allow lists could expose runtime details to clients.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The feature has token and IP checks, but the code captures request debug context and can emit it through X-Debug-Info when enabled.

content.value_statement: Distributed failures are hard to reproduce across services. This skill helps configure tracing, logging, profiling, dashboards, and production-safe debugging workflows.
actual_capabilities: Designs local and remote debugging workflows for Node.js services.
Outlines OpenTelemetry tracing with spans, trace IDs, and service metadata.
Defines structured debug logging with console, file, and Elasticsearch transports.
Provides profiling patterns for CPU profiles, heap snapshots, and slow functions.
Describes debug dashboards, IDE launch settings, and production debugging controls.
limitations: Examples need security review before use in production.
It does not validate live infrastructure or network exposure.
It assumes JavaScript and Node.js patterns in many examples.
It cannot replace incident response or observability platform expertise.

use_cases.title: Trace Service Failures
use_cases.description: Add trace boundaries, correlation IDs, and span metadata across related services.

use_cases.title: Standardize Debug Logging
use_cases.description: Create consistent debug logs, metadata fields, and sampling controls for teams.

use_cases.title: Prepare Production Diagnostics
use_cases.description: Plan controlled profiling, dashboards, and emergency debug procedures for production issues.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Basic Debugging
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a debugging setup for my Node.js service. Include IDE settings, useful logs, and safe development defaults.

prompt_templates.title: Add Trace Coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Design OpenTelemetry tracing for these services: [services]. Include span boundaries, correlation IDs, and safe attribute rules.

prompt_templates.title: Create Profiling Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a profiling workflow for CPU and memory issues in [service]. Include sampling, storage, access controls, and cleanup.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Debugging
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this production debugging plan for security risks, data leaks, exposed ports, and operational safeguards: [plan].

output_examples.input: A team needs to diagnose slow requests across checkout, payment, and inventory services.
output: Trace boundaries are defined at each service entry point.
Trace IDs are added to logs and response headers.
Request bodies are excluded from spans unless explicitly redacted.
Sampling is reduced for production and increased during incidents.

output_examples.input: An SRE wants a production profiling plan for memory growth.
output: Heap snapshots are gated by authorization and IP allow lists.
Snapshot files are written to a restricted directory.
Retention and cleanup rules are documented.
The plan avoids exposing inspector ports to public networks.

best_practices: Bind remote debuggers to localhost unless a secure tunnel is used.
Redact secrets, request bodies, and personal data before logging or tracing.
Store profiles and heap snapshots with strict access controls and retention limits.
anti_patterns: Do not expose inspector ports on 0.0.0.0 in production.
Do not place untrusted debug messages into the DOM with innerHTML.
Do not enable verbose tracing without sampling, redaction, and storage limits.

faq.question: What systems does this skill target?
faq.answer: It focuses on Node.js services, distributed tracing, debug logging, profiling, dashboards, and IDE debugging workflows.

faq.question: Can it be used for production debugging?
faq.answer: Yes, but production examples require strong authentication, redaction, sampling, and network restrictions before use.

faq.question: Does it install observability tools?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation guidance and examples that users must adapt and run themselves.

faq.question: Does it support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What data should be excluded from traces?
faq.answer: Exclude secrets, tokens, passwords, raw request bodies, session identifiers, and personal data unless safely redacted.

faq.question: What is the main security concern?
faq.answer: The examples include remote debugging and debug data collection patterns that can be unsafe without strict controls.
